label: Symmetric Spaces
notes: This chapter, printed pages 299 to 341, presents symmetric spaces of non-compact type as the richest concrete family of CAT(0) spaces. We motivate the geodesic-reversing symmetry at each point, name the central example of positive-definite matrices, and preview flats, rank, and the Tits boundary as recurring organising ideas.

label: The Point Symmetry
notes: A symmetric space carries at every point an isometry that reverses every geodesic through that point. We emphasise that this single axiom forces homogeneity, completeness, and an analytic Lie-theoretic structure. Stress that the symmetry is local data with global consequences, distinguishing these spaces from arbitrary homogeneous Riemannian manifolds.

label: Three Types
notes: De Rham and Cartan split symmetric spaces into compact, Euclidean, and non-compact type. We care about non-compact type because exactly there the sectional curvature is non-positive, giving Hadamard manifolds that are CAT(0). Make clear that compact-type factors carry positive curvature and are excluded from our comparison-geometry programme.

label: P(n) of Positive Matrices
notes: Introduce the model space P(n) of positive-definite symmetric matrices as an open convex cone. Explain that it is the universal example: every non-compact symmetric space embeds totally geodesically inside some P(n). The point symmetry at the identity is inversion, and at any A it is conjugated inversion, fixing A.

label: SL(n,R)/SO(n)
notes: Show that the general linear group acts transitively on P(n) by congruence, with the orthogonal group stabilising the identity. Hence P(n) is the homogeneous space GL(n)/O(n), and its trace-one slice is SL(n,R)/SO(n). Emphasise that geometry is now group theory: invariant tensors descend from the Lie algebra.

label: Invariant Metric and Geodesics
notes: Define the invariant Riemannian metric at the identity by the trace form on symmetric matrices, transported by the group action. Geodesics through A take the form t maps to A exp(tX) A-transpose. Stress that the matrix exponential, not straight lines in the ambient space, parametrises the genuine geodesics of this curved cone.

label: Distance and Eigenvalues
notes: The invariant distance between two positive matrices is the root-sum-of-squares of the logarithms of their generalised eigenvalues. We connect this to solving the generalised eigenvalue problem and to the logarithm of the relative matrix. Highlight that logarithms convert multiplicative spectral data into an additive Euclidean-flavoured distance.

label: Non-Positive Curvature
notes: Explain why P(n) is a Hadamard manifold: it is complete, simply connected, and has non-positive sectional curvature, computed from brackets of symmetric matrices. By Cartan-Hadamard it is therefore CAT(0). Underscore that convexity of the distance function and unique geodesics are the payoff we will reuse repeatedly.

label: Flats and Rank
notes: A flat is a complete totally geodesic isometrically embedded Euclidean subspace. In P(n) flats arise from maximal abelian subalgebras of symmetric matrices, the simultaneously diagonalisable directions. The rank is the maximal flat dimension; for P(n) it equals n minus one on the trace-one slice. Emphasise rank as the obstruction to hyperbolicity.

label: Cartan Decomposition
notes: State the Cartan decomposition of the Lie algebra into symmetric and antisymmetric parts, and the polar form writing any element as orthogonal times exponential of diagonal. The Weyl group permutes eigenvalues, cutting each flat into chambers. Make the link between abstract decomposition and the concrete diagonalisation students already know.

label: Tits Boundary and Buildings
notes: For rank at least two the boundary at infinity, with the Tits angular metric, is a spherical building: apartments are boundaries of flats glued along chambers. We contrast this with the rank-one case where the boundary is a featureless sphere. Stress that combinatorial rigidity emerges precisely in higher rank.

label: Synthesis
notes: Recap the dictionary: point symmetry gives homogeneity, non-compact type gives CAT(0), P(n) realises everything concretely, flats encode rank, and the Tits boundary becomes a building. Close by previewing how these spaces seed rigidity theorems and serve as the canonical higher-rank laboratory for non-positive curvature.
